title: Mirabuena bitungol: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Mirabuena bitungol: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Mirabuena bitungol is a governor's plum variety from Florinda Mirabuena. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Mirabuena is a registered bitungol variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Bi 01. Florinda Mirabuena bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Mirabuena bitungol is grown

blocks.text: Compare it with the others in our [governor's plum variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Mirabuena was about 15 to 20 years old and about 4 to 5 meters tall when it was registered. It bears every year, with fruit in Sept. Nov. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

A fruit of Mirabuena weighs about 13.2 grams, and its shape is globose. The flesh is purple and soft. Its sweetness measured 18.4 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 79.7 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is Sept. Nov, bearing annual.
Where and when to plant Mirabuena bitungol

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Mirabuena?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
